[[File:DecipherCon 2002 Day 1A pairings.jpg|thumb|right|260px|At the [[2002 World Championship]].]]
'''Andrew Howard''' (forum handle '''Yoda Killa''')<ref name="pcf-10-24">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=24#24 Countdown to SWCCG @ DecipherCon 2002 - 2 Days!], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (30 October 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040229131252/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=24%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> was listed as '''Tournament Support Advocate''' on the early swccgpc.com Advocate Council, succeeding [[John Arendt]] in that role.<ref name="swccgpc2002home">[https://web.archive.org/web/20021106101746/http://www.swccgpc.com/ The SWCCG Player's Committee], swccgpc.com (Wayback, 6 November 2002)</ref><ref name="council2002">[https://web.archive.org/web/20021209221742/http://www.swccgpc.com/council.htm Advocate Council], swccgpc.com (Wayback, 9 December 2002)</ref>

The Players Committee announced on 24 October 2002 that Howard was joining as the new Advocate for the Tournament Department, replacing [[John Arendt]].<ref name="pc-oct02">[http://www.swccgpc.com/Archives/october02archives.htm October Updates], swccgpc.com (24 October 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20030423222342/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/Archives/october02archives.htm Internet Archive]</ref> He received official word of the appointment about a week before [[DecipherCon 2002]], and on 30 October 2002 he and fellow Advocate [[Eric Olson]] left for Norfolk, Virginia, and the [[2002 World Championship]].<ref name="pc-dconwrap" /> Toward the end of 2002 he announced the four-tier 2003 Championship Circuit and an exclusive partnership between the PC and Decktech Inc. ([[DeckTech]]), whose co-sponsored DPC Championship Series let players qualify for the World Championships and win cash.<ref name="pc-rtw03">[http://www.swccgpc.com/News/Events/2003/roadtoworlds03.htm Road to Worlds Begins in 2003; SWCCG Player's Committee Announces Strategic Partnership], swccgpc.com (late 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040620161313/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/Events/2003/roadtoworlds03.htm Internet Archive]</ref> On 6 February 2003 he announced a swccgpc.com facelift (a frames format, a resource page, Advocate biographies and a Shadow Squadron volunteer database)<ref name="pc-feb03">[http://www.swccgpc.com/Archives/february03archives.htm February Updates], swccgpc.com (6 February 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20030423221707/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/Archives/february03archives.htm Internet Archive]</ref> and opened applications for the 2003 Championship Circuit, whose first SWCCG Open Qualifier was set for [[2003 MegaCon|MegaCon]] on 1 March 2003.<ref name="pc-champ0203">[http://www.swccgpc.com/News/championshipnews02062003.htm 2003 Championship Circuit Opens in One Month], swccgpc.com (6 February 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20030424053234/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/championshipnews02062003.htm Internet Archive]</ref> On 23 March 2003 he moved the start of the State, Provincial and National Championships to 1 May 2003, citing the transition of the PC's product to a new warehouse and the military action in Iraq, which had directly affected him.<ref name="pc-mar03">[http://www.swccgpc.com/Archives/march03archives.htm March Updates], swccgpc.com (23 March 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20030819162615/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/Archives/march03archives.htm Internet Archive]</ref> On 1 April 2003 he announced the opening of the PC's Online Affiliate Store with Universal Cards.<ref name="pc-apr03">[http://www.swccgpc.com/Archives/april03archives.htm April Updates], swccgpc.com (1 April 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20030810085606/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/Archives/april03archives.htm Internet Archive]</ref> In June 2003 he and Eric Olson were the project managers of a PC subcommittee developing independent tournament management software.<ref name="pc-tsw03">[http://www.swccgpc.com/News/tournamentchanges06182003.htm Upcoming Changes to Decipher's Tournament Software; How does it affect you?], swccgpc.com (18 June 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20030809102648/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/tournamentchanges06182003.htm Internet Archive]</ref>

On the Players Committee forum he signed his posts "Cheers, Andrew Howard".<ref name="pcf-10-24" /> On 30 October 2002, as Player Advocate for Tournament Support, he posted the Committee's schedule for [[DecipherCon 2002]] and the full list of Day 2 qualifiers for the [[2002 World Championship]],<ref name="pcf-10-24" /> and announced the [[Classic]] format playtest tournament that [[Scott Lingrell]] would run there on 1 November 2002.<ref name="pcf-9-23">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=23#23 SWCCG Player's Committee to Debut "Classic Format"], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (30 October 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041228093720/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?t=9 Internet Archive]</ref> On 7 December 2002 he announced the Classic Format "Winter Celebration" contest for tournament directors and Squadron Members who ran Classic tournaments between 14 December 2002 and 31 January 2003, with Premiere uncut sheets as prizes, and thanked Lingrell for running the first Classic tournament at DecipherCon.<ref name="pcf-360-5124">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=5124#5124 Player's Committee Announces Winter Contest], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (7 December 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040318152804/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=5124%26amp Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="pcf-359-5123">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=5123#5123 Player's Committee Announces Winter Contest], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (7 December 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040318153123/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=5176%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> On 29 December 2002 he said that the decklists of [[Jason Kilby]], the 2002 Young Jedi World Champion, would be posted on swccgpc.com the next day; they were up by the first week of January 2003.<ref name="pcf-489-7174">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=7174#7174 YJ World Champion], Shadow 31, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (19 December 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040330205638/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=10543%26amp Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="pcf-489-7566">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=7566#7566 YJ World Champion], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (29 December 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040330205638/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=10543%26amp Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="pcf-489-8840">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=8840#8840 YJ World Champion], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (7 January 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040330205638/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=10543%26amp Internet Archive]</ref>

On 28 January 2003 he defended the forum's rule against posting dream cards.<ref name="pcf-750-12680">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=12680#12680 Polite Reminder], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (28 January 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050228113751/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=12576%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> He ran the Players Committee's first live online coverage of an event, posting updates from the [[2003 DPC Chicago]] weekend on the forum from 10 to 12 April 2003.<ref name="pcf-1290-23801">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=23801#23801 DPC Chicago Coverage begins NOW!], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (10 April 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040625212948/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=23884%26amp Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="pcf-1295-23848">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=23848#23848 Live Coverage UPDATE #1], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (11 April 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040625210814/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=23848%26amp Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="pcf-1299-23883">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=23883#23883 Live Coverage UPDATE #4], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (12 April 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040131132845/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?t=1299%26amp Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="pcf-1302-23893">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=23893#23893 Live Coverage UPDATE #5], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (12 April 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040625214828/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=23900%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> In April 2003 he wrote that he was the Players Committee's Advocate rather than a "Decipher Tournament Advocate", and that his full attention went to keeping SWCCG alive, since [[Young Jedi]] had fewer than ten sanctioned tournaments a month worldwide and the [[Jedi Knights Trading Card Game]] had had about none since the 2002 World Championships.<ref name="pcf-526-24534">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=24534#24534 Do people want events for Young Jedi at Cons this year?], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (22 April 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040925201053/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=24508%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> In May 2003, when players asked what would become of the card images on Decipher's site, he wrote that he already had all of them and that hosting had been arranged in case Decipher took them down.<ref name="pcf-1448-25417">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=25417#25417 following on from what GO was saying...], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (9 May 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041120152757/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=25407%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> On 15 May 2003 he asked players for their views on the new Classic Starting Effects, noting that earlier versions had been harsher.<ref name="pcf-1487-26039">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=26039#26039 New Starting Effects for Classic], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (15 May 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040126055136/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?t=1487%26amp Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="pcf-1487-26160">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=26160#26160 New Starting Effects for Classic], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (15 May 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040126055136/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?t=1487%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> From 4 June 2003 he deleted all forum topics that had had no posts in the previous 60 days, to reduce clutter and loading times.<ref name="pcf-1674-28428">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=28428#28428 Cleaning up the Forums], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (3 June 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040229131701/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=28590%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> In August 2003 he locked a thread asking for Jedi Knights virtual cards, writing that Young Jedi and Jedi Knights were "pretty much gone" and that virtual cards for them were not his decision.<ref name="pcf-1973-31340">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=31340#31340 YJ World Championship Results?], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (5 August 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040928104229/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=31154%26amp Internet Archive]</ref>

At Dragon*Con 2003 he told players that "insert" cards were legal in Classic, and the official Classic ban list was updated to match.<ref name="pcf-2197-33349">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=33349#33349 Are inserts allowed classic], Nick Kolnik, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (18 September 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040928104140/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=33349%26amp Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="pcf-2197-33355">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=33355#33355 Are inserts allowed classic], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (19 September 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040928104140/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=33349%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> On 18 September 2003, after stepping down, he wrote that he had been at all the major conventions and had run all the big events, including the World Championships of 2002 and 2003, always at his own expense, since the Players Committee did not have the funds; on 20 September he wrote that he was no longer part of the Classic decision-making.<ref name="pcf-2188-33299">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=33299#33299 New Tournament Advocate], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (18 September 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040112231657/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=36534%26amp Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="pcf-2197-33412">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=33412#33412 Are inserts allowed classic], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (20 September 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040928104140/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=33349%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> In December 2003 he wrote that the new DecipherCon would be held at GenCon every year, at least for the next few years, and that the SWCCG World Championship was separate from DecipherCon and GenCon, although it could be held at GenCon in 2004.<ref name="pcf-2500-38568">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=38568#38568 Deciphercon 2003], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (11 December 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040115051041/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=38698%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> In April 2004 he wrote that most of the remaining SWCCG players were tournament players, the reverse of the game's prime,<ref name="pcf-3078-44071">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=44071#44071 Is this game dead??], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (4 April 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040427135016/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=44074%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> and that the game was in more trouble than when the license was lost.<ref name="pcf-3180-44988">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=44988#44988 SWCCG worlds and more], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (18 April 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040709185410/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=45251%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> In May 2004 he wrote that he had always been against "random" contests that let people design virtual cards.<ref name="pcf-3279-46173">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=46173#46173 Decktech and V cards], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (10 May 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040625210908/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=46730%26amp Internet Archive]</ref>
